argument_summary: The supportable position is not clean certification without qualification. It is certification on aggregate launch-readiness evidence, conditioned on explicit disclosure that Spanish-language refund guidance is a named launch context with missing evaluation coverage and unknown multilingual performance in that area. The admissible record supports general launch readiness through aggregate threshold clearance, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general support/latency/rollback checks, but it also shows those checks do not cover the named Spanish-language refund context. On that record, the defensible packet narrows the claim: certify the model for launch readiness generally, while stating that Spanish-language refund guidance remains unevaluated and must not be represented as validated.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation cost may be real, but it is not needed to justify the packet if the packet is narrowed to caveated certification. The admissible basis for minimizing escalation is that the existing record can support a bounded, disclosed certification outcome without overstating multilingual coverage.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy text, as provided here, permits general readiness evidence to support launch readiness but requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed. It does not support a statement that the named Spanish-language refund context is passed or has no known limitation. The compliant interpretation is therefore caveated certification with explicit disclosure of the gap and unknown status, not an unqualified no-limitation certification.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification with no deployment limitation for Spanish-language refund guidance.
General readiness, latency, rollback, and rehearsal evidence do not validate the named Spanish-language refund context.
If the actual certification artifact omits the explicit disclosure of the Spanish-language refund eval gap and unknown status, the certification position would not satisfy the stated policy.
